Cigna Shares Rise as Third-Quarter Earnings Beat Estimates and 2026 Profit Outlook Increases
sum: Cigna Group (NYSE:CI) shares gained 1.5% in premarket trading on Thursday after the US health insurer reported third-quarter earnings and revenue above analysts' expectations and raised its adjusted earnings guidance for 2026.

The company reported adjusted earnings of $7.98 per share, exceeding the consensus estimate of $7.52. Quarterly revenue increased 6% year over year to $73.7 billion, compared with analysts' expectations of $72.65 billion.
Cigna also increased its full-year adjusted earnings forecast to $30.60 per share, up $0.15 from its previous guidance and above the market consensus of $30.51.
Cigna generated third-quarter revenue of $73.7 billion, representing a 6% increase from the corresponding period last year.
The result exceeded analysts' revenue forecast of $72.65 billion by approximately $1.05 billion.
Adjusted earnings per share reached $7.98, compared with the consensus estimate of $7.52, a difference of $0.46 per share.
The results reflected revenue growth across the company's two principal operating businesses, Evernorth Health Services and Cigna Healthcare.

Cigna Group stock faces an earnings test on November 5
sum: The Cigna Group stock is heading toward the company's third-quarter earnings release on Thursday, November 5, before the U.S. market opens. A Yahoo Finance analysis, originally published by Barchart, says analysts expect diluted earnings per share to decline from the year-ago quarter despite continued longer-term earnings growth.
Cigna Group stock traded at 266.65 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:40 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. Investors can use the real-time quote of Cigna Group stock for the latest trading indication.

The preview puts the immediate focus on the September quarter. Analysts expect diluted earnings per share of 7.46 U.S. dollars, down 4.7 percent from 7.83 U.S. dollars a year earlier. The company has nevertheless beaten Wall Street's earnings estimates in each of the four preceding quarters, raising the importance of the November release for the near-term investment case.

For full-year 2026, analysts cited by the preview expect earnings per share of 30.50 U.S. dollars, compared with 29.84 U.S. dollars in 2025. Their projection rises to 33.46 U.S. dollars for 2027. The contrast between softer quarterly earnings and higher annual estimates leaves medical-cost trends, customer retention and the profitability of contracts as central issues for investors.

The Cigna Group serves more than 185 million customer relationships across more than 30 markets and jurisdictions, according to the same analysis. Its business combines Cigna Healthcare with Evernorth Health Services. The company also introduced Health Sense on October 6, a personalized support model intended to connect health information, benefits, costs and clinical expertise. The initial focus is oncology and cardiometabolic care, with rollout planned from early 2027.

The initiative is intended to reduce inefficient healthcare spending by 10 percent by 2030, according to the cited analysis. That longer-term efficiency goal offers a strategic counterweight to the near-term earnings test, but the November report will give investors the next direct indication of operating performance and management's outlook.
Broader healthcare and market sentiment can be followed in the S&P 500 market reports.

What Happened With UnitedHealth Stock This Week?
sum: Shares of UnitedHealth Group (UNH) rose 4.5% over the two trading days through Wednesday, October 14, while the S&P 500 fell 1.1%. The company reported fiscal Q3 2026 results before the market opened on Tuesday. The stock slipped 0.2% that day before posting its gain on Wednesday. Management also raised its forecast for full-year 2026 earnings. So what did the report change for someone who owns the shares?
Fiscal Q3 2026 earnings per share came in at $4.69, clearing the $4.18 analysts expected. Revenue matched estimates almost exactly at $113 billion. The surprise was in profit, not sales.
On Tuesday, the market treated the report as little news. The S&P 500 was nearly flat. UnitedHealth moved alongside CVS Health and Cigna, which also edged lower, while Elevance Health rose.

Through fiscal Q2 2026, UnitedHealth’s operating margin, the share of revenue left after the costs of running the business, returned above its level a year earlier. The margin was 4.6% in fiscal Q2 2025. It fell to 3.8% in fiscal Q3 2025 and 0.3% in fiscal Q4 2025. This margin decline occurred during a year of growing sales. In FY2025, UnitedHealthcare, the largest segment, grew revenue 15.7%, and Optum Rx grew 16.1%.

The margin then recovered to 8.0% in fiscal Q1 2026 and 7.1% in fiscal Q2 2026. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue grew only 0.4%, so the extra profit came from keeping more of each dollar rather than selling more. On a twelve-month view, profit has not come back. Diluted earnings per share were $15.54 in the twelve months to June 2026, down from $23.08 a year earlier.

Management now expects more from 2026 than it did three months ago. On October 13, the company raised its full-year 2026 forecast for GAAP diluted earnings per share to at least $19.50, up from $18.70 in July. A forecast is not a result.
Management credited the quarter to discipline and execution across every part of the business.

The Cigna Group’s Forward P/E Signals Value. Earnings Risks Remain
sum: The Cigna Group (NYSE:CI) brings together its Cigna Healthcare insurance business and Evernorth Health Services, which covers pharmacy benefit management and specialty pharmacy operations. By diversifying its business in this way, Cigna can generate earnings from several sources. As a result, we added the company to our best blue-chip dividend stocks list.

However, the company still faces challenges such as regulatory scrutiny, pricing pressure, and rising healthcare costs. In the second quarter of 2026, Cigna's revenue grew 7% from the previous year, reaching $71.7 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) climbed to $7.78, up from $7.20, and net income came in at $1.66 billion. Management expressed their confidence in continued growth by raising the 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to at least $30.45.Even with stronger earnings, some risks remain. For example, Cigna Healthcare's medical care ratio increased to 84.5% from 83.2% a year earlier, which means medical costs took up a larger portion of premiums.
Evernorth is also dealing with regulatory pressure on pharmacy benefit management and could see its margins squeezed as the industry changes how it handles rebates and drug pricing.

The Cigna Group (NYSE:CI) trades at a forward P/E ratio of 8.26, compared to a trailing P/E of 11.41. This difference shows that the market expects Cigna's earnings to rise. With a forward P/E of 8.26, the implied earnings yield is around 12.1%, compared with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield of 5.21% on October 13, 2026. This represents a spread of approximately 6.9 percentage points, although equity earnings are uncertain and do not represent guaranteed cash returns. Of course, equity earnings aren't guaranteed cash returns, so this kind of comparison is more illustrative than direct.

Cigna's valuation has narrowed over time. According to Yahoo's data, its forward P/E was 11.26 in June 2025 and dropped to 8.87 by September 2025. Right now, Cigna's forward P/E is lower than CVS Health's 10.67, which suggests that Cigna is trading at a relative discount. However, it's important to keep in mind that the two companies differ in their business mix and risk profiles, which can affect direct comparisons.

Is The Health Insurer Rebound Complete? Some Seem To Think So
sum: The health insurance industry, dogged by high medical costs from an influx of patients needing medical care, may finally have turned the corner.

An increasing number of industry analysts and company disclosures are indicating costs are under control for the likes of CVS Health, Centene, Cigna, Elevance Health, Humana, UnitedHealth Group and others.

Take a report last week from Morningstar senior analyst Julie Utterback, who predicted these managed care organizations "may rebound and boost profit growth well above norms through 2030" following what she called "recent troughs."

The cost picture for health insurers should become a little more clear next month when companies start reporting their third quarter earnings. Investors and analysts who follow the companies are hoping the third quarter brings more of what companies reported in the second quarter.

UnitedHealth Group, parent of the nation's largest health insurer in UnitedHealthcare, reported more than $5 billion in second quarter net income. That came during a period this year when UnitedHealthcare's medical care ratio continued to fall.

"The second quarter 2026 medical care ratio was 86.7% compared to 89.4% in the second quarter 2025," the company said of the ratio, which is the percentage of premium revenue that goes toward medical costs. "The year-over-year decrease was driven by benefit design and pricing discipline, member mix and medical cost management initiatives."

Diversified healthcare companies like UnitedHealth, CVS Health, Cigna, Elevance Health and Humana are also hearing good news in more controversial areas of their businesses like pharmacy benefit management. Such PBMs have faced new federal and state rules and regulations and it wasn't long ago that analysts on Wall Street were speculating the vertical integration strategy of these healthcare giants would go away.

items.t: Why Cigna (CI) Stock Is Up Today
sum: Shares of health insurance company Cigna (NYSE:CI) jumped 3.5% in the afternoon session after analyst firm Bernstein raised its price target on the stock to $381 from $371, citing a positive outlook. Bernstein maintained its "Outperform" rating on Cigna.

The firm's optimism is based on the company's ability to manage medical costs and the strong performance of its Evernorth division. Analysts at the firm also projected a better-than-consensus medical loss ratio, which is a key measure of profitability for health insurers, and forecasted a 9.5% adjusted earnings per share growth rate through 2030. The new price target suggests significant potential upside from the stock's previous closing price.
The shares were trading at $304.26, up 3.7% from the previous close.
Is now the time to buy Cigna? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

Cigna's shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 9 months ago when the stock dropped 14.3% on the news that the company reported underwhelming third-quarter results. Revenue grew 9.5% year-on-year to $69.75 billion, beating estimates by 3.6%.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $7.83, which was 2.5% ahead of the consensus forecast. However, the positive results were overshadowed by concerns about profitability and future growth. The company's operating margin declined to 3% from 4% a year ago, continuing a multi-year downward trend in profitability. Additionally, while Cigna's full-year earnings guidance was in line with expectations, forecasts for revenue growth over the next 12 months point to a significant slowdown. This, combined with a slight dip in customer numbers from the previous quarter, likely prompted investors to look past the quarterly beat and focus on potential challenges ahead.
